name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run the 72-hour dual-prompt A/B test with 15% of users, forcing feed. This tests whether the new prompt routing improves engagement without relying on user opt-in, giving us a cleaner signal. The trade-off is frustrating 15% of users with an unwanted feed change, but the forced test cuts noise from self-selection bias. If the new prompts win, we roll it out to everyone; if not, we scrap it and avoid a worse rollout.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t 15% churn—it’s that forcing the feed *confounds the prompt’s signal* by mixing routing changes with UX friction. A better alternative: run the A/B test on *opt-in users only*, then compare engagement lift to the forced cohort. Settle it by checking if the opt-in group’s signal aligns with the forced group’s—if not, the forced test is noise.
